mean: to find joy in helping others
lit: to take helping people as one's pleasure

use.how: Describes a person's character, as a predicate or before 的: 他一向助人为乐；助人为乐的精神。 It takes no object. Said of everyday, willing helpfulness.

near.diff: 见义勇为 is bravely stepping in when someone is in danger; 助人为乐 is ordinary, cheerful helpfulness with no risk involved.

cue: A retired neighbour spends every weekend fixing other people's bikes for free and says it makes her day. How do you describe her?

ctx.s: 我的邻居王阿姨一向{助人为乐}，谁家有事她都去帮忙。
ctx.en: My neighbour Auntie Wang has always loved helping; whenever a family has a problem, she goes over to help.

ctx.s: 学校表扬了几位{助人为乐}的同学。
ctx.en: The school commended several students who are always glad to help others.

ctx.s: 他退休后在社区免费教孩子下棋，说{助人为乐}比什么都开心。
ctx.en: After retiring he teaches the neighbourhood kids chess for free, and says nothing makes him happier than helping.

ctx.s: 我们应该从小培养孩子{助人为乐}的品质。
ctx.en: We should nurture a love of helping others in children from an early age.

ctx.s: 这位出租车司机常常免费送老人去医院，真是{助人为乐}的好榜样。
ctx.en: This taxi driver often takes elderly people to hospital for free; he's a real example of kindness to others.

ctx.s: 网上那篇文章讲了一个快递员{助人为乐}的故事，感动了很多人。
ctx.en: That article online told the story of a courier who loves helping people, and it moved a lot of readers.

bad.s: 谢谢你昨天{助人为乐}我搬家。
bad.en: (meant: thanks for helping me move yesterday)
bad.why: It describes a person's character and takes no object. Just thank them for helping, using the plain verb bang.

bad.s: 他冲进大火救出了小孩，真是{助人为乐}。
bad.en: (meant: he rushed into the fire and saved a child; how heroic)
bad.why: Risking your own safety to save someone in danger calls for jian yi yong wei; this idiom is for everyday kindness.

mean: give an inch and they take a mile
lit: having gained an inch, to push on for a foot

story.text: Dictionaries trace the phrase to the strategist Fan Ju, who advised King Zhaoxiang of Qin to befriend distant states and attack nearby ones, because then every inch of land taken would be the king's inch and every foot the king's foot. There it praised steady, secure gains; the idiom later came to mean never being satisfied with what one has been given.

use.how: Predicate, often in warnings: 别得寸进尺！ Said of someone who, after a concession, keeps demanding more. It takes no object.

near.diff: 贪得无厌 is insatiable greed in general; 得寸进尺 is pushing for more right after someone has given way.

cue: You let your flatmate borrow your bike for an afternoon; now they've kept it a week and are asking for your car as well. What are they doing?

ctx.s: 我借给他一百块，他又要借两百，真是{得寸进尺}。
ctx.en: I lent him a hundred yuan and now he wants to borrow two hundred more. Give him an inch and he takes a mile.

ctx.s: 你已经晚交了三天，现在还想再拖一周？别{得寸进尺}了！
ctx.en: You're already three days late and now you want another week? Don't push your luck!

ctx.s: 孩子：“再玩十分钟好不好？”妈妈：“刚才已经多给你十分钟了，不许{得寸进尺}。”
ctx.en: Child: "Can I play ten more minutes?" Mum: "I already gave you ten extra minutes. Don't push it."

ctx.s: 对方一开始只要求降价一点，我们答应后，他们却{得寸进尺}，要求免费送货。
ctx.en: At first they only asked for a small discount; once we agreed, they pushed for more and demanded free delivery too.

ctx.s: 如果你一直让着他，他只会{得寸进尺}。
ctx.en: If you keep giving in to him, he'll just keep asking for more.

ctx.s: 邻居先是把车停在我家门口，后来{得寸进尺}，干脆把杂物也堆了过来。
ctx.en: First the neighbour parked in front of my house; then, emboldened, he started piling his junk there too.

bad.s: 她学习很努力，成绩{得寸进尺}，越来越好。
bad.en: (meant: she studies hard and her grades keep improving step by step)
bad.why: It does not mean steady progress; it criticises someone who keeps demanding more after a concession.

bad.s: 他总是{得寸进尺}别人。
bad.en: (meant: he always takes advantage of other people)
bad.why: It takes no object. Say simply that he is always pushing for more (ta zongshi de cun jin chi), and name the people in a separate clause.

mean: to stand by and do nothing to help
lit: to tuck one's hands into one's sleeves and watch from the side

story.text: In his funeral address for his friend Liu Zongyuan, Han Yu wrote that when a clumsy man does the carving, his fingers bleed and his face runs with sweat, while the skilled craftsman stands by with his hands drawn into his sleeves. He was lamenting that a man of Liu's talent had been left on the sidelines. The image became the idiom for watching without lending a hand.

use.how: Predicate, very often negated: 我不能袖手旁观。 Said of someone who could help with a problem but chooses not to.

near.diff: 见死不救 is far stronger: leaving someone in mortal danger; 袖手旁观 is any failure to pitch in when help is needed.

cue: Your teammates are racing to fix a bug before the deadline, and one colleague just leans back and watches without lifting a finger. What is he doing?

ctx.s: 朋友有困难，我怎么能{袖手旁观}呢？
ctx.en: My friend is in trouble; how could I just stand by and watch?

ctx.s: 弟弟在搬家，哥哥却坐在沙发上{袖手旁观}，一点忙都不帮。
ctx.en: The younger brother was moving house, and his older brother just sat on the sofa watching, not helping at all.

ctx.s: 公司出了问题，你作为经理却{袖手旁观}，这说不过去吧？
ctx.en: The company is in trouble and you, the manager, are just watching from the sidelines. That's hard to justify, isn't it?

ctx.s: 村里修路，每家都出了力，没有一个人{袖手旁观}。
ctx.en: When the village built the road, every family pitched in; not one person stood aside.

ctx.s: 看到有人在地铁里欺负老人，乘客们没有{袖手旁观}，纷纷上前制止。
ctx.en: When someone started harassing an old man on the subway, the passengers didn't just look on; they stepped in one after another to stop it.

ctx.s: 他说：“这件事我不能{袖手旁观}，明天我去找校长谈谈。”
ctx.en: He said, "I can't just stay out of this. Tomorrow I'll go and talk to the head teacher."

bad.s: 我昨天在公园{袖手旁观}了一场足球比赛，很精彩。
bad.en: (meant: yesterday I watched a football match in the park; it was great)
bad.why: It is not neutral watching; it blames someone for not helping when help is needed.

bad.s: 谢谢你在我最困难的时候{袖手旁观}。
bad.en: (meant: thank you for standing by me in my hardest time)
bad.why: It criticises refusing to help, the opposite of standing by someone. Thank them for their support instead.

mean: to abandon those who helped once they are no longer needed
lit: to tear down the bridge once one has crossed the river

use.how: Predicate or before 的: 他过河拆桥；过河拆桥的人。 It takes no object. Said of someone who drops or turns on the people who helped them succeed.

near.diff: 忘恩负义 is ingratitude in general; 过河拆桥 is discarding helpers precisely once they have served their purpose.

cue: As soon as the start-up turns a profit, its founder cuts out the early investor who kept it alive in the lean years. What did the founder do?

ctx.s: 他升职以后就不理当初帮过他的同事了，真是{过河拆桥}。
ctx.en: After his promotion he ignored the colleagues who had helped him. Talk about kicking away the ladder.

ctx.s: 我帮你找到了工作，你现在却说我坏话，这不是{过河拆桥}吗？
ctx.en: I helped you find this job and now you're badmouthing me. Isn't that just using me and throwing me away?

ctx.s: 做人不能{过河拆桥}，别人帮过你，你要记在心里。
ctx.en: You mustn't turn your back on people once they've helped you; remember who helped you.

ctx.s: 项目一成功，公司就把出力最多的合作方换掉了，大家都说他们{过河拆桥}。
ctx.en: As soon as the project succeeded, the company replaced the partner who had done the most. Everyone said they'd ditched them once they were no longer needed.

ctx.s: “放心吧，我不是那种{过河拆桥}的人。”
ctx.en: "Don't worry, I'm not the kind of person who forgets you once I've got what I need."

ctx.s: 小说里的那个商人发财后{过河拆桥}，最后再也没人愿意跟他合作。
ctx.en: The merchant in the novel turned on those who had helped him once he got rich, and in the end nobody would work with him.

bad.s: 为了考上大学，他{过河拆桥}，辞掉工作专心复习。
bad.en: (meant: he burned his boats, quitting his job to focus on the exam)
bad.why: Cutting off your own retreat is po fu chen zhou; this idiom is ingratitude towards the people who helped you.

bad.s: 他发财以后就{过河拆桥}了我。
bad.en: (meant: once he got rich he dropped me)
bad.why: It takes no object; the person dropped is introduced with dui before it.

mean: to step in bravely to help someone in danger
lit: seeing what is right, to act on it bravely

story.text: In the Analects, Confucius says: to see what is right and not do it is to lack courage. The idiom turns the saying round into praise for those who do act. Today it is the standard phrase in news reports and official awards for bystanders who intervene in a crime, fire or accident.

use.how: Predicate or before 的: 他见义勇为；见义勇为的青年。 Common in news and awards. Said of a bystander who takes a risk to stop a crime or save a life.

near.diff: 助人为乐 is everyday, cheerful helpfulness; 见义勇为 is a brave act in a dangerous moment.

cue: On a busy street, a passer-by tackles a man snatching an old woman's bag and holds him down until the police arrive. What did the passer-by do?

ctx.s: 他跳进河里救起了落水的孩子，大家都称赞他{见义勇为}。
ctx.en: He jumped into the river and rescued a drowning child; everyone praised his courage.

ctx.s: 公交车上有人偷钱包，一位年轻人{见义勇为}，当场抓住了小偷。
ctx.en: Someone was stealing a wallet on the bus; a young man bravely stepped in and caught the thief on the spot.

ctx.s: 市里给这位{见义勇为}的外卖小哥颁发了奖金。
ctx.en: The city gave a cash award to the delivery rider who bravely stepped in.

ctx.s: 新闻报道了三名中学生{见义勇为}、帮邻居扑灭大火的事迹。
ctx.en: The news reported how three secondary-school students bravely helped their neighbours put out a big fire.

ctx.s: 我们提倡{见义勇为}，但也要注意保护自己的安全。
ctx.en: We encourage people to step in bravely, but they should also take care to keep themselves safe.

ctx.s: 记者问他为什么{见义勇为}，他说：“当时没想那么多。”
ctx.en: When the reporter asked why he had risked himself to help, he said, "I didn't think about it at the time."

bad.s: 同事帮我复印了文件，真是{见义勇为}。
bad.en: (meant: my colleague kindly photocopied the documents for me)
bad.why: Far too grand: it is for brave acts in danger. For a small favour, call the person kind and helpful (rexin).

bad.s: 警察每天上班都在{见义勇为}。
bad.en: (meant: police officers act bravely every day at work)
bad.why: It praises a bystander who steps in of their own accord, not someone doing their job.

mean: saying one thing while meaning another
lit: the mouth says yes while the heart says no

use.how: Predicate or before 的: 他口是心非；口是心非的人。 Criticises insincerity; between friends it can also tease someone who hides what they really want.

near.diff: 阳奉阴违 is outwardly obeying orders while secretly disobeying; 口是心非 is any gap between what one says and what one really thinks.

cue: Your friend insists she doesn't mind you going to the party without her, then sulks all evening. What is she being?

ctx.s: 我讨厌{口是心非}的人，有意见就直说。
ctx.en: I can't stand people who say one thing and mean another; if you have an objection, say it.

ctx.s: 她嘴上说不想要礼物，其实心里很想要，真是{口是心非}。
ctx.en: She says she doesn't want a present, but she really does. Saying one thing, meaning another.

ctx.s: “你说不生气，可你脸都红了，别{口是心非}了。”
ctx.en: "You say you're not angry, but your face has gone red. Stop pretending."

ctx.s: 他说支持我的计划，背后却跟老板说不行，原来是{口是心非}。
ctx.en: He said he backed my plan, but behind my back told the boss it wouldn't work. He never meant it.

ctx.s: 孩子说“我不饿”，眼睛却一直盯着蛋糕，有点{口是心非}。
ctx.en: The child said "I'm not hungry", but kept staring at the cake. Not quite meaning what he said.

ctx.s: 那位经理在会上要求大家节约，自己却天天大吃大喝，员工都觉得他{口是心非}。
ctx.en: That manager tells everyone at meetings to economise, yet wines and dines every day himself; the staff think he doesn't mean a word of it.

bad.s: 我中文不好，常常{口是心非}，说错话。
bad.en: (meant: my Chinese is poor, so I often say the wrong thing)
bad.why: It means being insincere on purpose, not making slips of the tongue.

bad.s: 他是个{口是心非}的人，说到做到。
bad.en: (meant: he is a man of his word who means what he says)
bad.why: It means the opposite: words that do not match one's real thoughts. A sincere person is xin kou ru yi.

lit: to gulp like a wolf and swallow like a tiger

use.how: Predicate, or adverbial with 地: 狼吞虎咽地吃完了。 Describes how a person or animal eats: fast and greedily, usually from hunger or haste.

cue: After a twelve-hour shift with no break, a nurse sits down and gets through her whole dinner in two minutes. How did she eat?

ctx.s: 弟弟饿坏了，一回家就{狼吞虎咽}地吃起饭来。
ctx.en: My little brother was starving; the moment he got home he started wolfing down his dinner.

ctx.s: 慢点吃，别{狼吞虎咽}的，对胃不好。
ctx.en: Eat slowly, don't gobble your food like that; it's bad for your stomach.

ctx.s: 爬了一天山，大家坐下来{狼吞虎咽}，一会儿就把饭菜吃光了。
ctx.en: After a whole day of climbing, everyone sat down and tucked in so fast that the food was gone in no time.

ctx.s: 他中午只有十分钟休息，只能{狼吞虎咽}地吃完午饭。
ctx.en: He only gets a ten-minute break at noon, so he has to bolt his lunch.

ctx.s: 小狗一看到狗粮，马上{狼吞虎咽}起来。
ctx.en: As soon as the puppy saw its food, it started gulping it down.

ctx.s: 医生提醒他，{狼吞虎咽}容易发胖，吃饭要细嚼慢咽。
ctx.en: The doctor warned him that bolting food makes you put on weight, and that he should chew slowly.

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜很{狼吞虎咽}。
bad.en: (meant: the food at this restaurant is delicious)
bad.why: It describes the way someone eats, not the food itself. Just say the food is delicious (haochi).

bad.s: 他是个很{狼吞虎咽}的人，什么都想要。
bad.en: (meant: he is a greedy person who wants everything)
bad.why: It only describes eating fast, not greed in general, and it is not a character adjective after hen.

mean: to be alarmed or amazed by something quite ordinary
lit: to be greatly startled and find strange what is small

use.how: Predicate, often 别大惊小怪 or 有什么好大惊小怪的。 Criticises an exaggerated reaction of surprise or alarm, such as exclaiming or fussing, to something normal.

near.diff: 小题大做 is treating a small matter as serious and over-reacting with action; 大惊小怪 is the exaggerated surprise or alarm itself.

cue: A friend shrieks and calls everyone over because the waiter served her tea in a glass instead of a cup. How is she reacting?

ctx.s: 只是一只小虫子，你别{大惊小怪}的。
ctx.en: It's just a little bug; don't make such a fuss.

ctx.s: 外国人用筷子有什么好{大惊小怪}的？现在很多人都会。
ctx.en: What's so amazing about a foreigner using chopsticks? Lots of people can these days.

ctx.s: 奶奶第一次看到扫地机器人，{大惊小怪}地叫了起来。
ctx.en: The first time Grandma saw the robot vacuum, she cried out as if it were a marvel.

ctx.s: 我只是剪了个短发，同学们却{大惊小怪}，围着我问个不停。
ctx.en: I only had my hair cut short, but my classmates acted as if it were huge news and crowded round asking questions.

ctx.s: 南方人看到下雪往往很兴奋，北方人却觉得没什么好{大惊小怪}的。
ctx.en: Southerners often get excited when they see snow, but northerners think it's nothing to get worked up about.

ctx.s: 新来的同事看到老板穿拖鞋上班，有点{大惊小怪}，其实这在我们公司很正常。
ctx.en: The new colleague was rather startled to see the boss come to work in slippers, but that's perfectly normal at our company.

bad.s: 妹妹{大惊小怪}那只小蜘蛛。
bad.en: (meant: my sister made a huge fuss about that little spider)
bad.why: It takes no object. Say she made a fuss when she saw it: kan dao zhizhu jiu da jing xiao guai.

bad.s: 听说他中了大奖，我们都{大惊小怪}。
bad.en: (meant: we were all amazed to hear he had won the big prize)
bad.why: It implies the surprise is unwarranted because the thing is ordinary. For genuinely big news say da chi yi jing.

mean: to treat a minor matter as a major issue
lit: to write a big piece on a small topic

use.how: Predicate, often 别小题大做 or 有点小题大做了。 Criticises excessive measures, fuss or punishment over something trivial.

near.diff: 大惊小怪 is exaggerated surprise or alarm; 小题大做 is blowing a small matter up into a big one, usually through what one does.

cue: Because someone left a coffee cup in the meeting room, your manager calls an all-staff meeting and writes a formal report. What is the manager doing?

ctx.s: 不就是迟到了五分钟吗？你别{小题大做}。
ctx.en: I was only five minutes late. Don't make a big deal of it.

ctx.s: 为了一张停车罚单就要请律师，是不是有点{小题大做}了？
ctx.en: Hiring a lawyer over a parking ticket? Isn't that a bit over the top?

ctx.s: 孩子打碎了一个杯子，他爸爸却罚他一个月不准看电视，太{小题大做}了。
ctx.en: The boy broke a cup and his father banned him from TV for a month. That's way out of proportion.

ctx.s: 有人认为学校因为一句玩笑就开除学生，是{小题大做}。
ctx.en: Some people think expelling a student over a single joke is blowing things out of proportion.

ctx.s: “这只是个小问题，我们自己修就行，没必要{小题大做}去找工程师。”
ctx.en: "It's only a small problem; we can fix it ourselves. No need to make a big thing of it and call an engineer."

ctx.s: 网上有人为了一个错别字写了上千字的批评，大家都说他{小题大做}。
ctx.en: Someone online wrote over a thousand words of criticism over a single typo, and everyone said he was making a mountain out of a molehill.

bad.s: 他做事很认真，连小事也{小题大做}，值得我们学习。
bad.en: (meant: he is conscientious and takes even small things seriously; we should learn from him)
bad.why: It is always a criticism of over-reaction, never praise for care. Say he takes even small things seriously (renzhen).

bad.s: 我们公司从小做起，后来{小题大做}，成了大企业。
bad.en: (meant: our company started small and grew into a big enterprise)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with growing from small to big; it means making too much of a trivial matter.

use.how: Predicate, adverbial with 地, or in 一副满不在乎的样子。 Describes an attitude of total unconcern, usually about something one ought to care about. It takes no object: 对……满不在乎。

near.diff: 漫不经心 is doing something carelessly, without attention; 满不在乎 is not caring about a problem, criticism or consequence.

cue: Your teenage son has failed three exams; when you bring it up he just shrugs, says "whatever" and goes back to his game. How is he acting?

ctx.s: 妈妈批评他，他却一副{满不在乎}的样子。
ctx.en: His mum told him off, but he looked as if he couldn't care less.

ctx.s: 考试没及格，她{满不在乎}地说：“下次再考呗。”
ctx.en: She failed the exam and said, without a care, "I'll just take it again next time."

ctx.s: 你丢了钱包怎么还这么{满不在乎}？
ctx.en: You've lost your wallet; how can you be so unbothered?

ctx.s: 别人都在担心台风，只有他{满不在乎}，照样出门钓鱼。
ctx.en: Everyone else was worried about the typhoon; only he didn't care at all and went fishing as usual.

ctx.s: 他表面上{满不在乎}，其实心里很难过。
ctx.en: On the surface he acts as if he doesn't care, but inside he's really upset.

ctx.s: 对于网上的批评，这位作家显得{满不在乎}，继续按自己的方式写作。
ctx.en: The writer seemed completely unbothered by the criticism online and went on writing in her own way.

bad.s: 你想喝茶还是咖啡？我{满不在乎}。
bad.en: (meant: tea or coffee? Either is fine with me)
bad.why: It describes indifference to something that matters and sounds rude here. Say dou xing or wu suo wei.

bad.s: 他{满不在乎}这次考试。
bad.en: (meant: he doesn't care about this exam at all)
bad.why: It takes no object; the thing not cared about is introduced with dui before it.
